summary: Client-side retry middleware reorders function/tool calls on resume causing duplicate side-effects when prefix cache diverges
description:
Issue summary:
Customer using the Go SDK with a custom retry middleware (wraps SDK stream client to implement exponential backoff + local batching) observes duplicate external tool executions (webhook posts and DB writes) after stream resume following transient network disconnects.

Impact:
Intermittent duplicate side-effects in production for a small subset of long-running chat sessions (~0.2% of sessions). Customer reports duplicated webhook payloads and duplicate order rows in their downstream DB leading to reconciliation work and customer complaints.

Environment:
- Redwood Dedicated pool (dedicated tenant), prod us-east
- Go SDK v0.12.3 with custom RetryMiddleware v1.0 (in-house)
- Model routes pinned to redwood-alpha-2b, fallback to open-llama-13b enabled

Steps to reproduce (customer repro):
1) Start a long-lived streaming chat session that triggers two sequential function/tool calls: (a) external webhook POST to create a ticket, (b) internal DB write confirmation. The SDK client sends both functool frames in a short window.
2) During the second token window, simulate a brief network disruption (TCP reset / client Internet flaps).
3) Client retry middleware closes and then re-establishes the SDK stream. On resume the middleware attempts to replay the buffered frames but in some runs reorders the buffered batch (due to sorting by retry-time heuristics) so the DB write appears before the webhook confirmation frame.
4) Redwood serving runtime processes the resumed stream; because the model fallback path returns a shorter prefix cache (KV cache divergence) the server accepts the replayed frames as new, causing the webhook to be executed again. DB write also happens a second time in the interleaved order.

Observed logs & artifacts:
- Customer provided debug trace: https://slack-redwood.slack.com/archives/C012XYZ/p1640000000
- Customer reproduction capture: s3://slatemaps-repro/trace-20260313.tar.gz (contains SDK trace, local middleware logs)
- Server logs around the time show two separate funcall-request ids: funcall_id=fc_9a7b... and fc_9a7b...-r2; timestamps separated by ~1s.
- Serving runtime trace shows fallback to open-llama-13b during resume with shorter kv_cache.sequence=42 vs original 46.

Initial hypothesis:
- The customer-side retry middleware mutates ordering of buffered functool frames during resume which, combined with a model fallback that results in shorter prefix/KV cache at the server, prevents the runtime from matching the replay to the original in-flight execution. Without a canonical dedup token preserved across resume and fallback, the server treats the replay as a new request and re-executes side-effects.

Investigation notes so far (support/SRE):
- Reproduced a minimal repro locally by running the Go SDK with the customer's middleware that reorders based on a last-attempt-first heuristic. Confirmed duplicate webhook post in dedicated staging.
- Checked server-side dedup windows: dedup tokens are scoped to per-model-version + kv_cache.sequence range; when fallback occurs the dedup lookup can miss if kv_cache.sequence decreased.
- Confirmed SDK does send an idempotency header for funcalls in normal flows but the middleware code rewrites headers during replay (it drops the original idempotency-baggage and generates a new short token).

Immediate mitigations suggested to customer:
- Hotfix: stop mutating idempotency baggage on replay and preserve the original funcall idempotency token across retries/resume.
- Workaround: disable in-client batching/reordering for long-running sessions (recommended until server-side tolerance fix is in place).

Next steps / action items:
- Support: Confirm customer has patched middleware to preserve idempotency baggage and test for duplicates (assigned to Liam Chen).
- SRE/Runtime: Evaluate changing dedup lookup policy to include broader kv_cache ancestry window when checking for previous funcall executions across model fallback boundaries (engineering task; create RFC).
- Product: Consider adding guidance to SDK docs about not reordering functool frames and an SDK helper to preserve idempotency baggage across retries.

Priority rationale:
Customer is on Dedicated plan and experiencing production-side duplicates; P1 chosen due to business impact and potential data integrity issues.
